page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-12xCPU-24GB is a Cloud Native family virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 12 shared x86_64 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 24.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance type, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance trade-off between single-core and multi-core operations. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance falls into the bottom 10% with a score of 784.69, reflecting the shared nature of the vCPUs and the 2.0 GHz clock speed. Conversely, multi-core performance scales to average levels, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 9386.85 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 11354.0. Memory bandwidth benchmarks show average performance, reaching 60.68 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 40.05 GB/sec for large-block write operations.

In terms of workload execution, the server demonstrates average capabilities across standard tasks, achieving 17.86 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and a static web serving throughput of 9.63 GB/sec. For language model tasks, the server handles prompt processing for a 7B model at 42.65 tokens per second, but text generation drops to a lower rate of 6.21 tokens per second. Qualitatively, the shared CPU allocation provides a cost-efficient option for multi-threaded workloads that do not require sustained, dedicated single-core performance, such as distributed web serving, software compilation, and parallel text or image processing.

Given its shared CPU architecture and 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio, this server offers a qualitatively cost-efficient profile for multi-threaded workloads such as parallel software compilation, static web serving, and basic database operations that do not demand dedicated single-core execution.
